text: Let's define the words we'll keep using. A problem is a task we want done — for example, find the largest of three numbers. A solution is the idea of how to do it — compare them and keep the biggest one. An instruction is a single, precise step the computer can actually carry out. A program is the complete, ordered set of those instructions. And programming is the process of creating that program — taking a solution from your head and turning it into exact steps a computer can follow. So hold on to one distinction from the very start: programming is the process; a program is the result of that process.
